content: To prevent smoke detectors from being triggered, sensitive electronic equipment must not be directly sprayed during disinsection procedures. The crew must be thoroughly familiar with the disinsection process before it begins. During the disinsection process and for five minutes after spraying is completed, the aircraft’s air-conditioning system must remain turned off. Recirculation fans may remain operational if they are essential for the aircraft's functioning, but they should be set to the lowest flow rate. When closing the lower cargo doors, leave them slightly open to allow placement of the aerosol cans in a secure, upright position. Activate the lock-down nozzles of the aerosols. Once the aerosols are confirmed to be functioning correctly, immediately close the cargo hold door to complete the disinsection process. If the cargo hold needs to be reopened (except for loading animals) or if an aerosol malfunction occurs, the entire procedure must be repeated. Allow seven minutes after activating the aerosols before loading animals into the cargo hold. Used aerosol containers should remain in the lower cargo holds and be retrieved by ground handlers at the destination airport. These containers must be accessible to ground handlers. If an airline opts to remove aerosol containers before departure, the containers must be carried onboard along with the disinsection certificate. Retrieval of the containers should only occur seven minutes after activation. The door of the disinsected cargo hold must be opened only to the minimum extent necessary to retrieve the used containers and then immediately closed to prevent recontamination. The cargo hold should only be opened for loading animals and closed immediately afterward to avoid recontamination. Any non-compliance with the disinsection procedures must be reported to the intended first port of arrival before the aircraft lands. For freighter aircraft, manual spraying of the cargo hold must be conducted at the last departure airport after all cargo has been loaded. Non-essential personnel must vacate the cabin and cargo areas before disinsection begins. Aerosols must be discharged into each cargo hold in a manner that ensures all areas are treated. If certain areas of the aircraft are inaccessible due to cargo, aerosols should be discharged into the center of the aircraft, directed toward the ceiling above the cargo, or positioned evenly on top of the cargo when using single-shot aerosols. After spraying is completed, allow at least five minutes for the spray to settle before departure. For residual disinsection treatments, the cabin and cargo hold should be treated in conjunction. Residual treatment must be performed at a maximum interval of eight weeks and completed whenever the aircraft is available. The formulation used for residual spraying is 2% permethrin emulsifiable concentrate (EC). Aerosol formulations containing 2% permethrin aqueous emulsion (AE) should be used for areas like the flight deck, cockpit, and crew rest areas where liquid emulsions could pose safety risks or damage the aircraft. Before residual spraying, the aircraft should be configured to ground service mode. All lockers, cupboards, and storage units must be opened, cleared, and cleaned, while curtains and window blinds should be closed. Carpet covers should be removed. The air-conditioning system, including preconditioned air from ground support units, must be turned off. Recirculation fans may remain on if essential but should be set to the lowest flow rate. All surfaces, including floors, ceilings, walls, lockers, curtains, toilets, and galley areas, must be sprayed. Doors and locker lids must be sprayed on both sides, and floor areas should be resprayed afterward. Care must be taken to avoid spraying food preparation areas, seats, mirrors, windows, medical equipment, and removable galley components. Any spray spilled on these areas must be immediately wiped clean, and food-contact surfaces must be additionally cleaned with soap and water. For cargo holds, all areas must be free of cargo, pallets, containers, and debris before spraying. Walls, ceilings, floors, and both sides of dividing curtains must be sprayed, with particular attention to sidewall and floor cavities. The crew must be informed before cargo hold spraying begins. Sensitive electronic equipment must not be directly sprayed, and the crew must be fully aware of the procedures to avoid triggering smoke detectors. Certification of disinsection treatments must comply with ICAO standards and recommended practices. Both residual and aerosol disinsection treatments require completion of ICAO Annex 9 documentation. Copies of the residual disinsection certificate and the General Declaration must be provided. If disinsection has not been conducted, the pilot in command or authorized agent must notify the relevant authorities at the arrival airport before landing. This allows local authorities to supervise or perform on-arrival disinsection if necessary. Passengers with medical conditions that could be affected by on-arrival disinsection treatments may be allowed to disembark before the procedure, leaving their belongings onboard. This exemption is subject to local procedures and is commonly practiced in countries like Australia and New Zealand. After the disinsection treatment, exempted passengers may retrieve their belongings from the cabin once all other passengers have disembarked. On-arrival cabin spraying procedures require all exterior doors and windows to remain closed until directed otherwise by local authorities. Cabin crew must prepare the cabin by opening all overhead lockers and ensuring passengers remain seated. During spraying and for five minutes afterward, the aircraft’s air-conditioning system must remain off. Recirculation fans may remain on if essential but should be set to the lowest flow rate. Spraying should begin at the rear of the cabin, with the operator walking along the aisle at a controlled pace, directing the spray toward open overhead lockers and the ceiling. All galleys, toilets, and crew rest areas must be sprayed, with care taken to avoid spraying aircraft equipment or personnel. A five-minute saturation period must be observed after spraying before the air-conditioning system is turned on and airflow maximized. Passengers must remain seated during this time until clearance to disembark is granted by local authorities.
